extraction.name: MathQA
extraction.description: A large-scale dataset of 37k English multiple-choice math word problems covering multiple math domain categories, annotated with operation programs corresponding to each problem. It enhances the AQuA dataset with fully-specified operational programs using a new operation-based representation language.
extraction.creator: Aida Amini, Saadia Gabriel, Shanchuan Lin, Rik Koncel-Kedziorski, Yejin Choi, Hannaneh Hajishirzi
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created by annotating problems from the AQuA dataset with formal operation programs using a dynamic crowd-sourcing annotation platform. Annotators iteratively selected operations and arguments, with quality control strategies including accuracy thresholds and validation by at least 2 out of 3 validators.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Problems that are unsolvable, near-duplicates with incorrect solutions, or require reasoning not yet modeled by neural networks were excluded. Only 61% of automatically annotated problems passed human validation, so automatic annotations were not included.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The AQuA-RAT dataset, which provides over 100K GRE- and GMAT-level multiple-choice math word problems with rationales across a wide range of domains.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowd workers annotated math word problems with formal operation programs using a dynamic annotation platform. Annotators sequentially selected operations and arguments, with intermediate results calculated automatically. Quality control included random evaluation through pre-defined test questions with an accuracy threshold; annotations from annotators dropping below the threshold were marked untrusted. A validation strategy required at least 2 out of 3 validators to rank a program as valid.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Validation accuracy of 94.64% across categories. Expert evaluation of 500 problems showed 92% of annotations are valid, with 87% agreement between expert validation and crowdsourcing validation. Agreement between human annotators on categorization was 84%, and their agreement with the model was 74.5%.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: At least 3 validators per item (2 out of 3 required to mark as valid)
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: An automatic dynamic programming approach was experimented with to generate operation programs using numbers in AQuA rationales, but was not included in the final dataset due to noise (only 61% passed human validation).
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The AQuA dataset contains statistical bias that the proposed representation language can help reduce.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The AQuA dataset contains significant noise including problems with incorrect solutions, problems unsolvable without brute-force enumeration, and rationales missing required solution steps. The dataset also includes currently unsolvable problems such as sequence and high-order polynomial problems.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is suited for training deep-learning models to solve math word problems, as well as testing and validating sequence-to-program models for mathematical reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Annotation expansion using Levenshtein distance to find similar problems, replace numeric values with generic numbers, and expand annotations. Dataset randomly split 80/12/8% for training/dev/test.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Dynamic annotation platform used to annotate math word problems with formal operation programs. Quality control through pre-defined test questions with accuracy thresholds; annotations below threshold labeled as untrusted. Alignment validation requiring at least 2 out of 3 validators to rank a program as valid (94.64% validation accuracy). Automatic annotation via dynamic programming was excluded due to noise.
